messages:
Anya: quick design check — attaching the adaptive SLO knob mock and a couple of pool affordance options. wondering about clarity for burst vs reserved and how the cost pulse should behave when someone drags the knob :eyes: 
Mike: looked. love the live cost pulse but worried it competes visually with the SLO label. can we tone it down (lighter bg, 2px border) and move the numeric estimate to the right?
Jess: +1 on moving estimate. also language: instead of `Burst` can we use `On-demand burst` or `Temporary burst`? engineers keep mixing burst with reserved GPUs. microcopy should signal duration.
Ben: technical note — burst is implemented as short-lived spot allocations. we should avoid implying permanence. suggest copy: "On-demand burst (short-lived)" and tooltip: "Adds temporary capacity for up to X minutes".
Anya: good call. Sam, accessibility check: does the SLO slider announce values properly with screen readers? and keyboard granularity?
Sam: checked with VoiceOver. current slider announces "SLO 80%" but not the guardrail state. need aria-live region to announce when a guardrail warning appears (e.g., "Min exceeds budget"). keyboard: use arrow keys for 1% step, shift+arrow for 5%. add aria-valuetext = "SLO 80 percent — within budget" or "— exceeds budget".
Jess: also think about focus order. pool selector should come before min/max inputs so people pick capacity target before adjusting limits. otherwise they may set min without a pool.
Mike: UI affordance: for pool tiles, add a small badge showing "capacity type: shared/dedicated" and a tiny cost-per-hour line. clickable area must be full tile (not just title) for mobile.
Ben: implementation caveat: when user increases min beyond current pool capacity, prompt inline with a small suggested action: "Increase pool quota" button. don't send them to a modal unless they click it.
Anya: copy proposal for the SLO tooltip: "SLO sets the target latency percentile we prioritize. Lower SLO may reduce cost but increase tail latency." Shorten if needed.
Jess: nit: keyboard label should be explicit: "SLO target percent (lower = faster responses)" — avoids ambiguity for new users.
Sam: color contrast: the green success color for within-guardrail doesn't meet AA at small sizes. either use darker green or add an icon + text.
Mike: agree — icon + text is good. maybe a subtle checkmark when within budget, and an amber warning icon when guardrail triggers.
Anya: design decision needed: when guardrail triggers do we prevent submit or allow but show a persistent warning? my preference: allow with explicit confirmation and a short rationale CTA.
Ben: tech wise allow + confirm is easier for rollout. we can log an event for the override.
Jess: UX flow for overrides: show inline short message with "Proceed anyway — I understand the cost implications" + secondary "Adjust to fit budget". both should be accessible via keyboard.
design-bot: mock uploaded to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/adaptive-slo-knob — frame names: "Knob-final-v2", "Pool-tiles-affordance".
Anya: next steps: incorporate copy changes (On-demand burst label + tooltip), move cost estimate to right, add aria-live announcements, and update pool tile badge. I'll iterate and ping for another quick sweep tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Sam: will add a11y checklist to the PR and run quick axe scan once mocks land.
Mike: I'll prototype the darker contrast states and the inline quota CTA.
Jess: will draft the microcopy variants for copy review doc.
Ben: I'll verify edge cases where min > pool cap and send a short list of error states.
Anya: perfect — thanks team.
